outcome: Complicated malaria (severe thrombocytopenia, hepatic dysfunction, severe anaemia)
cohort: The study included 323 hospitalized patients with complicated malaria (median age 20 years) from three endemic areas of the Colombian Pacific Coast enrolled between 2014 and 2016.
finding: The study identified a high prevalence of complicated malaria, with predominant complications being severe thrombocytopenia, hepatic dysfunction, and severe anaemia, noting that severe anaemia was most frequent in children with P. vivax and hepatic dysfunction in older patients with P. falciparum.
